description: A five by five Conway's Game of Life with every cell readable, settable and patchable on its own, stepped by a clock jack; the grid wraps, so a pattern leaving one side returns on the other

params.text: Lets the clock jack step the grid; switched off, the grid changes only through the buttons, the cell jacks and the four pattern buttons
Copies the pattern now on the grid into the stored pattern
Puts the stored pattern back onto the grid
Sets every cell alive or dead at random, an even chance each
Turns that cell on if it is off and off if it is on

inputs.text: Steps the grid one generation on each rising edge above 1V, provided the clock switch is on
Copies the pattern now on the grid into the stored pattern on each rising edge above 1V
Puts the stored pattern back onto the grid on each rising edge above 1V
Sets every cell alive or dead at random on each rising edge above 1V
Sets every cell dead on each rising edge above 1V
Turns that cell on if it is off and off if it is on, on each rising edge above 1V

outputs.text: Carries 10V while that cell is alive and 0V while it is dead

notes: the grid comes up empty and stays dark until something is put on it: press Restore for the stored pattern, which on a new module is a glider, or press Random
a cell stays on with two or three neighbours on, switches on with exactly three and goes off otherwise; neighbours are counted across the edges, so the grid behaves as a torus
each trigger jack is added to the button beside it before the trigger is worked out, so holding that button down stops the jack from firing again
this module offers its memory to an expander: the running grid as one channel and the stored pattern as a second, reached by an Accessor or DMA-FX placed immediately to its left
